newsitem.title: UK: Brent rallies again, other N. Sea crudes steady.
newsitem.headline: Brent rallies again, other N. Sea crudes steady.

text.p: Brent crude continued to rise in a quiet market on Wednesday, gaining some 10 cents in the past three days on the back of demand from the United States, traders said.
Two physical Brent cargos, loading May 8-10 and May 12-14 changed hands, both at June Brent -27 cents. This compared with a Brent May 4-6 cargo sold at June Brent - 37 cents on Monday.
Other European grades seemed to have hit a peak for the time being. A May 19-21 Forties traded at Dated Brent +20 cents. Traders said two more deals, probably Norwegian grades, traded on a p+c basis.

One European broker said there was talk of some Ekofisk moving, at Dated Brent +15 cents or so on Wednesday. One May 8-10 Troll cargo was sold into the U.S. Gulf at dated flat on Tuesday, traders said.
A European major was heard offering a May 13-15 Brent cargo and a second seller said it will offer a May 12-14 cargo on Thursday adding the price will be indicated then.
The only Brent cargo to turn physical on Wednesday was kept before the five o'clock deadline by Esso, traders said. The cargo is due to load in the May 15-17 period.
On the cash market, June Brent gained a little in late trade after maintaining a slightly downward slant during most of the morning and afternoon trade on Wednesday.
June Brent was trading six cents higher at $18.67 a barrel by 1728 GMT. It briefly hit a low of $18.48 after the NYMEX open.
The Brent paper market was also quiet with intermonth spreads and contracts for difference changing little.
A Jun/Jul changed hands at -8 cents. Outright June Brent paper was traded twice at $18.59 and once at $18.60.
Brent CFDs were broadly steady in thin trade. Two May 5-9/May 12-16 rolls were done at flat and an average May versus an average June traded at -15 cents.
Mediterranean refiners said good margins from sour crudes meant Urals would hold at current firm levels although buying was thin.

Tuesday's trades at dated -$1 and dated -96 cents were repeatable with only one 80Kt Urals cargo seen offered. The upcoming scheduled maintenance on Berth 2 at Novorossiisk would result in "erratic at best" Urals loadings.
Iraqi Kirkuk crude for May was now sold out, traders said. Liftings for the month were up on April at 13.5 million barrels, lifters said.
A cargo offered for sale on Tuesday at the equivalent of a 40-50 cent premium to the OSP was now being kept for the owners own system, they added.
West African barrels were pretty much cleared out and the 3-4 Forcados cargoes left for sale were not actively being offered.
"With the force majeure no-one really knows when or if they are going to load in May," one lifter said.
Other grades available included a cross month Brass River, an end May N'Kossa a Qua Iboe around May 20. -H. Haddadin/S. Hayden, London newsroom +441715428145
